expectations.text: PR.md tells the reviewer where to look first (the window filter or the limit comparison in rate.js) with a risk note
expectations.evidence: The 'Where to look first' section lists "`rate.js:6`, the expiry comparison `t - x < windowMs`" with the risk note "(logic)... Check this is the boundary you want".

expectations.text: PR.md includes evidence from running node test.js (pass count or output), and a section saying what was not verified (or states nothing unverified with a reason)
expectations.evidence: The Evidence section shows "$ node test.js / rate tests passed (4 assertions)", and a '## Not verified' section lists things that weren't checked, such as "No before/after against the old code."

expectations.text: PR.md states whether the change is easy to roll back (one-way or two-way door) or its blast radius
expectations.evidence: The 'Merge danger' section says "**Two-way door.** ... a revert restores the old behaviour. Blast radius: every caller of `createLimiter`."
